title: Transversal non-Clifford gates on good quantum locally testable codes
authors: Yiming Li, Zimu Li, Zi-Wen Liu
abstract: We achieve nontrivial transversal logical multi-controlled-$Z$ gates with asymptotically optimal parameters simultaneously on quantum low-density parity check codes and quantum locally testable codes, by applying the gate framework of [arXiv:2604.01874] to the recent good qLTC construction of [arXiv:2609.20780]. To this end, we use the covering space method to construct a nonzero cup product pairing on a finite arithmetic cubical complex. This differs from the previous construction of almost-good codes, whose base space is a hypergraph product. We express the pairing as a coefficient in a product of Moore determinants and prove polynomial nonvanishing by a bipartite multigraph specialization. We then construct covering spaces to obtain an asymptotic family of good qLTCs on which the pulled-back pairing induces the desired nontrivial transversal logical action.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous mathematical framework to construct quantum error-correcting codes, specifically qLDPC and qLTCs, capable of supporting transversal non-Clifford gates. By employing advanced tools from algebraic topology, such as cup product pairings on cubical complexes, the authors prove the existence of such codes with optimal parameters. This is a major theoretical advance for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The core problem is constructing quantum error-correcting codes that can support nontrivial transversal logical non-Clifford gates while maintaining optimal error-correction parameters.
main_result: The authors prove the existence of asymptotically good quantum LDPC and qLTC codes that support nontrivial transversal logical multi-controlled-Z gates for any required gate depth.
method: The method combines advanced algebraic topology (covering space method, cup product pairing on cubical complexes) with coding theory techniques to establish the necessary non-zero cohomology invariants.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum error-correcting codes, specifically quantum low-density parity check (qLDPC) codes and quantum locally testable codes (qLTCs). These codes are analyzed using algebraic structures derived from decorated Cayley cubical complexes.
key_observables: Nontrivial transversal logical multi-controlled-Z gates ($	ext{Cr}^{-1}	ext{Z}$), code parameters like constant rate, linear distance, and constant soundness.
important_parameters: The construction requires the existence of non-zero cup product pairings, which are proven by analyzing polynomial nonvanishing via bipartite multigraph specializations.
main_assumptions: The work builds upon previous constructions by applying a specific gate framework to recent good qLTC constructions, addressing compatibility issues arising from arithmetic identifications.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the necessary algebraic machinery (covering space method, cup product pairing) to guarantee the existence of non-zero invariants. It then applies this machinery to the specific structures of qLDPC and qLTCs to construct the required transversal gates.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the fundamental challenge of fault-tolerant quantum computation by providing explicit constructions for implementing non-Clifford gates on highly structured, good quantum codes.
